prompts.label: Hello Zig project
prompts.text:
I'm new to Zig. Create a minimal project from scratch.

- zig init-exe or zig init-lib and explain difference
- src/main.zig with std.debug.print("Hello, Zig!\n", .{})
- zig build run and zig build test commands
- Mention stable Zig 0.13+ / 0.14+ style if relevant

List files created and what build.zig does in one paragraph.

prompts.label: const var and integers
prompts.text:
Teach const vs var and integer types for a beginner.

- const fixed binding, var mutable
- i32, u64, usize for sizes
- @intCast example with overflow caution
- No implicit widening — explain briefly

Small main.zig with a counter loop using var.

prompts.label: Arrays and slices
prompts.text:
Explain arrays vs slices in Zig with string-like examples.

- const arr = [_]u8{ 1, 2, 3 } and slice arr[0..2]
- []const u8 as string slice, .len field
- Sentinel-terminated strings mention for C interop only

Show iterating with for (arr) |item|.

prompts.label: for and while loops
prompts.text:
Demonstrate for loops over slices and while with optional error capture.

- for (0..10) |i| and for (items) |x|
- while (condition) : (label) with break/continue
- Compare to C loops in 2 bullets

Include sum-of-slice exercise.

prompts.label: Error union try catch
prompts.text:
Introduce Zig error sets and error unions for beginners.

- const FileError = error{ NotFound, PermissionDenied }
- fn readConfig() FileError!Config with try in caller
- catch |err| switch handling
- Contrast with exceptions and Result<T,E> mentally

Runnable example reading a missing file path.

prompts.label: Optionals ?T and orelse
prompts.text:
Teach optional types ?T in Zig.

- if (maybe) |value| { } else { }
- orelse default value or return error
- @as for type coercion when needed
- Common mistake: double optional mention lightly

Example: findUser(id) ?User.

prompts.label: Structs and methods
prompts.text:
Define struct Point { x: f32, y: f32 } with methods distance and translate.

- pub fn on struct, self: *Self or self: Self
- Struct literal .{ .x = 1, .y = 2 }
- No inheritance — composition note in one sentence

Unit-style test in same file optional.

prompts.label: GeneralPurposeAllocator basics
Read file std.fs cwd
prompts.text:
Read a text file into memory using std.fs and an allocator.

- std.fs.cwd().openFile, readToEndAlloc or readFileAlloc
- defer allocator.free
- Handle error.FileNotFound in catch

Print first 200 chars safely.

prompts.label: Parse JSON std.json
prompts.text:
Parse JSON with std.json.parseFromSlice for a small struct.

- const User = struct { id: u32, name: []const u8 };
- Parse static string literal first, then file bytes
- defer parsed.deinit() pattern
- Mention strict typing vs dynamic Value when needed

Example JSON with two users.

prompts.label: HTTP server std.http
prompts.text:
Create a tiny HTTP server responding Hello on GET /.

- std.http.Server or current std API for your Zig version
- Listen on 127.0.0.1:8080, handle one request loop simply
- Test with curl

Note API drift between Zig versions honestly; prefer documented stable pattern.

prompts.label: Comptime if and types
prompts.text:
Introduce comptime for beginners with a max(T) style function.

- fn max(comptime T: type, a: T, b: T) T
- comptime if (@typeInfo(T) == .int) optional branch
- Explain compile-time vs runtime in plain language

Avoid full generic containers — keep one function.

prompts.label: Enums and tagged union
prompts.text:
Model Shape as enum or tagged union (circle | rectangle).

- fn area(shape: Shape) f64 with switch exhaustive
- Compiler error if case missing — highlight as feature
- Compare to Rust enum and Go without sum types

Small main printing areas.

prompts.label: Tests in same file
prompts.text:
Write test "addition works" and test "error on divide by zero" in Zig.

- test { try expectEqual(...); }
- zig build test command
- std.testing.expect, expectError

Place tests below main functions in one file.

prompts.label: build.zig targets and steps
prompts.text:
Explain build.zig for a beginner Zig executable project.

- b.addExecutable, install artifact, run step
- addLibraryImport for std only default
- zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast mention
- Where to add unit tests in build graph briefly

Annotate default build.zig sections.

prompts.label: C interop @cImport
prompts.text:
Call C printf or strlen from Zig using @cImport.

- @cInclude and linkSystemLibrary("c") in build.zig
- @cImport(@cInclude("string.h"))
- Explain @ptrCast and sentinel strings carefully

Minimal hello from C library.

prompts.label: HashMap std.HashMap
prompts.text:
Use std.HashMap for word frequency counting from a string.

- Key type []const u8 with appropriate context
- getOrPut, increment count
- Iterator over map entries
- Allocator required for map

Print top 5 words from sample paragraph.

prompts.label: Formatting std.fmt print writer
prompts.text:
Teach std.fmt.bufPrint and printing to stdout with placeholders.

- "User {s} has {d} points\n" format string
- Fixed buffer vs allocPrint for dynamic size
- fmt format specifiers {x}, {any} debug

Avoid alloc in hot path example using stack buffer.

prompts.label: Random numbers std.rand
prompts.text:
Generate random integers with std.Random and a PRNG (e.g. Xoshiro256).

- Seed from std.time.timestamp() for demo only — not crypto
- random.intRangeAtMost for dice roll 1..6
- Warn about crypto.random for secrets

Short dice simulation loop.

prompts.label: When to choose Zig checklist
prompts.text:
Give an honest beginner checklist: when Zig is a good fit vs C, Rust, or Go.

- Systems programming, C interop, explicit allocators strengths
- Smaller ecosystem and API churn caveats
- Learning path: C memory basics + build.zig + error unions

No flame war — bullet tradeoffs and one sample project idea (CLI tool).
